name: visualize
summary: A codebase in 3D: a scroll-driven walkthrough of how its parts work together (explain), or a code city of its files (render) -- one offline HTML file drawn with three.js

settings.summary: Where gt-visualize publishes a page by default: kept local, a claude.ai Artifact, a GitHub Pages folder, or a gist.
settings.detail:
local         the file stays on this machine  (default)
claude        a private claude.ai Artifact Claude publishes for you; updates keep the URL
github-pages  <repo>/<dir>/<slug>/index.html in a repo you name, pushed with your git login
gist          a secret (link) or public gist, with your gh login. GitHub shows a gist's
              HTML as source, not as a page

Every publish shows its plan (target, visibility, URL) and waits for your yes.
No credential is ever stored: the targets use the logins you already have.
Target details: gt_visualize.py targets set github-pages repo=... base_url=...

settings.summary: Who can see a published page by default -- checked against what the target can enforce.
